example.text: Consider a hypothetical sanitation worker who receives protective equipment and training before undertaking assigned work. question.answer: PPE can reduce immediate occupational exposure and training can improve safe practices, but lasting safety requires mechanised cleaning, accountable urban institutions, monitoring, health protection and livelihood support.

sections.heading: Safety as a dignity issue
paragraphs: The Press Information Bureau’s 10 November 2026 release presents the NAMASTE Scheme as a route from occupational risk to safer livelihood. It describes protective equipment and awareness training as practical interventions that can improve working conditions and support dignity.

sections.heading: Mechanism and limitation
paragraphs: PPE creates a protective barrier against hazards, while training helps workers recognise and avoid occupational risks. The release, however, is a beneficiary account and does not by itself establish scheme-wide coverage or prove that PPE alone replaces mechanised sanitation and enforcement.
